**Section IV: Essay (10 marks)**

*Write an essay of between 180 and 220 words on any one of the topics that follow.*

**Topic 1**

Consider yourself the leader of a students' association in your area. As a leader, how will you help or encourage your friends to go in for more challenging science subjects in school? Be precise in your effort to convince your friends.

questions.enonce_markdown: **Topic 1.** Write a speech, as the leader of your students' association, to encourage your friends to take up more challenging science subjects in school. Be precise in your effort to convince them. *(180 to 220 words)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un discours destiné à convaincre un auditoire de pairs (ici les amis de l'association) s'ouvre par une adresse directe (« Dear friends »), avance des arguments présentés dans un ordre croissant de force (« First..., Second..., Third..., Finally... »), et se referme sur un appel à l'action clair, jamais sur une simple récapitulation neutre.

**Modèle de le discours persuasif (speech) (180 à 220 mots) :**

Dear friends,

As the leader of our students' association, I have noticed that many of us avoid science subjects such as Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, calling them too difficult. I want to convince you to embrace these challenging subjects instead of running away from them.

First, science subjects open doors to careers our country urgently needs: doctors, engineers and researchers. Cameroon cannot develop without young people ready to fill these roles tomorrow.

Second, difficulty is not the same as impossibility. Many of our seniors who once struggled with these subjects later became successful scientists simply because they refused to give up. Their story proves that steady effort, not natural talent alone, makes the real difference.

Third, our association can organise weekly study groups where stronger students help weaker ones understand difficult notions such as chemical equations or algebra. Learning together removes fear and builds confidence for everyone.

Finally, let us change how we speak about these subjects. Instead of saying « Physics is too hard », let us say « Physics is challenging, and I can master it with effort. »

Dear friends, the future belongs to those who dare to face difficulty rather than avoid it. Let us take up this challenge together, starting this very term.

### Piège à éviter
Un texte qui énumère de bonnes raisons sans jamais s'adresser directement aux amis (« you », « we ») ressemble à un essai impersonnel et perd les points de forme attribués au registre attendu d'un discours persuasif.

### Conseil
Termine toujours un discours de ce type par une phrase d'appel à l'action précise (une date, une décision à prendre « dès ce trimestre ») plutôt que par une formule vague comme « I hope you understood », qui affaiblit l'impact persuasif du texte.
